front: In Amazon EBS, every gp3 volume includes a baseline of {{c1::3,000 IOPS}} in its storage price, at any size.
In Amazon EBS, one gp3 volume can be provisioned with up to {{c1::80,000}} IOPS.
extra: Before September 26, 2025 the maximum was [16,000 IOPS](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-gp3-max-iops-80000).

front: In Amazon EBS, one io2 Block Express volume on a Nitro instance supports provisioned IOPS {{c1::up to 256,000}}.
In Amazon EBS, io2 Block Express volumes are designed for {{c1::99.999 percent volume durability}}.
In Amazon EBS, the baseline IOPS of a gp2 volume grows at {{c1::3 IOPS per GiB}} of volume size.
In Amazon EBS, the throughput of one st1 volume is capped at a {{c1::maximum of 500 MiB/s}}.
In Amazon EBS, one Multi-Attach volume can attach to {{c1::up to 16 instances}} built on Nitro in the same Availability Zone.
In Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive, the {{c1::minimum archive period is 90 days}}; an earlier delete is billed for the remaining days.
In Amazon EBS, can you attach a volume to an instance in another Availability Zone?
back: No. Snapshot it and create a volume there.
extra: The volume and the instance [must be in the same Availability Zone](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-volume-same-az-as-instance). From a snapshot you can [create a duplicate volume in that zone](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-snapshot-restore-volume-other-az).

front: In Amazon EC2, does instance store data survive a stop and start of the instance?
back: No. A reboot keeps the data, but a stop erases it.
extra: Instance store data [persists even if the instance is rebooted](../facts/instance-store.md#instance-store-data-persists-reboot-not-stop), but not if the instance is [stopped, hibernated, or terminated](../facts/instance-store.md#instance-store-data-persists-reboot-not-stop).

front: In Amazon EBS, a medium-sized database does small random I/O and must cost little. Which volume type?
back: gp3.
extra: AWS names gp3 for a [balance between cost and performance](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-faq-gp3-suited-workloads), including medium-sized single-instance databases.

front: In Amazon EBS, a log processing job reads large files sequentially every hour. Which volume type?
back: st1, Throughput Optimized HDD.
extra: st1 fits [large, sequential workloads](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-st1-use-cases) such as log processing.

front: In Amazon EBS, can you turn on encryption for an existing unencrypted volume?
back: No. Snapshot it and create an encrypted volume from it.
extra: [You can't directly encrypt existing unencrypted volumes](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-encrypt-existing-volume-via-snapshot). From a snapshot you [create a new encrypted volume](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-encrypt-existing-volume-via-snapshot).

front: In Amazon EBS, can Elastic Volumes make a volume smaller?
back: No. Create a smaller volume and copy the data.
extra: [You can't decrease the volume size](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-volume-size-cannot-decrease). You [create a smaller volume](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-volume-size-cannot-decrease) and copy the data with a tool such as rsync.

front: In Amazon EBS, gp3 or gp2: which one ties its IOPS to the volume size?
back: gp2.
extra: With gp2, [performance scales with volume size](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-gp2-performance-scales-with-size). With gp3 you scale performance [independently of volume size](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-gp3-performance-independent-of-size).

front: In Amazon EBS, can an st1 or sc1 volume be a boot volume?
back: No. Use an SSD volume type.
extra: [Bootable st1 volumes are not supported](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-hdd-volumes-not-bootable), and [bootable sc1 volumes are not supported](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-hdd-volumes-not-bootable) either.

front: In Amazon EBS, cold data is scanned a few times a month and must cost as little as possible. Which volume type?
back: sc1, Cold HDD.
extra: sc1 has [the lowest cost per GB](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-sc1-lowest-cost-per-gb) of all EBS volume types.

front: In Amazon EBS, a database needs consistent sub-millisecond latency on one volume. Which volume type?
back: io2 Block Express.
extra: io2 Block Express gives [consistent sub-millisecond latency](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-io2-use-cases) for I/O-intensive databases.

front: In Amazon EBS, does a gp3 volume burst above its baseline performance?
back: No. You provision more IOPS instead.
extra: Every gp3 volume includes [3,000 IOPS](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-faq-gp3-no-burst) of steady performance and does not burst.

front: In Amazon EC2, root volume or other volume created at launch: which one is deleted on termination by default?
back: The root volume.
extra: The root volume is [deleted when that instance is terminated](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-delete-on-termination-root-default-true). Other volumes created at launch [are not deleted when that instance is terminated](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-delete-on-termination-additional-default-false).

front: In Amazon EBS, cluster software on several Nitro instances in one zone needs one shared block volume. What do you use?
back: An io2 volume with Multi-Attach.
extra: Multi-Attach lets you [attach a single Provisioned IOPS SSD](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-multi-attach-provisioned-iops-same-az) volume to instances [in the same Availability Zone](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-multi-attach-provisioned-iops-same-az).

front: In Amazon EBS, is XFS safe on a Multi-Attach volume that two instances mount?
back: No. Use a clustered file system.
extra: XFS and EXT4 are [not designed to be accessed simultaneously](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-multi-attach-needs-clustered-file-system), so you should [use a clustered file system](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-multi-attach-needs-clustered-file-system).

front: In AWS, Data Lifecycle Manager or AWS Backup: which one applies one policy across accounts and services?
back: AWS Backup.
extra: With AWS Backup you define one policy and [apply it across accounts and Regions](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-aws-backup-central-policy-across-accounts).

front: In Amazon EBS, can you share a snapshot that the AWS managed key aws/ebs encrypts?
back: No. Only a customer managed key allows sharing.
extra: [You can't share snapshots that are encrypted](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-snapshot-aws-managed-key-not-shareable) with the AWS managed key. You share snapshots [encrypted with a customer managed key](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-snapshot-aws-managed-key-not-shareable).

front: In Amazon EBS, volumes restored from a snapshot need full performance at once. What do you turn on?
back: Fast snapshot restore.
extra: A volume from such a snapshot is [fully initialized at creation](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-fsr-volume-fully-initialized-at-creation).

front: In Amazon EBS, can the newest snapshot still restore a volume after you delete the older snapshots?
back: Yes. The newest snapshot alone restores the volume.
extra: You need to [retain only the most recent snapshot](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-snapshot-deletion-keep-only-latest) to restore the volume.

front: In Amazon EBS, Recycle Bin or snapshot lock: which one stops a delete before it happens?
back: Snapshot lock.
extra: A locked snapshot [can't be deleted by any user](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-snapshot-lock-no-user-can-delete). Recycle Bin restores deleted [EBS volumes, EBS snapshots, and EBS-backed AMIs](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-recycle-bin-recovers-volumes-snapshots-amis).

front: In Amazon EBS, the volumes of an instance never reach their provisioned IOPS. What limits them first?
back: The EBS performance limit of the instance type.
extra: EBS performance is [bounded by the instance type's performance limits](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-instance-performance-bounded-by-smaller) or by the volumes, [whichever is smaller](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-instance-performance-bounded-by-smaller).

front: In Amazon EBS, does encryption by default encrypt the volumes you already have?
back: No. It covers new volumes and new snapshot copies.
extra: Encryption by default [has no effect on existing EBS volumes](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-encryption-by-default-new-resources-only).

front: In Amazon EBS, you need the backups of a volume in a second Region for disaster recovery. What do you do?
back: Copy the snapshots to that Region.
extra: You can [copy snapshots from one Region to another](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-snapshot-copy-cross-region-and-encrypt).

front: In Amazon EBS, can you read a snapshot through the Amazon S3 API?
back: No. Use the Amazon EC2 API.
extra: EBS snapshots are [only available through the Amazon EC2 API](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-faq-snapshots-not-via-s3-api).

front: In Amazon EC2, instance store or EBS volume: which one is included in the price of the instance?
back: Instance store.
extra: [There is no additional charge](../facts/instance-store.md#instance-store-no-additional-charge) for the instance store volumes that come with an instance.
